description:
Yuncha 1 is the name of a tea plant cultivar associated with Yunnan. 'Yun' stands for Yunnan and 'cha' for tea, and the number marks it as one of a numbered series of selections.

Little is documented about it in the open: who bred it, from what parents, when it was released, and what its leaf is like are all unclear. Do not confuse it with Yuncha Chunyun, a separately described Yunnan cultivar.

As a guide only, Yunnan greens tend to be fuller and more robust than those from eastern China, and they take slightly hotter water. Nothing specific to this cultivar can be said about taste.

If you see this name on a tea, ask the seller for the grower and the picking date, since the cultivar name alone tells you very little.
history: Little is documented about this cultivar. Its breeder, release date and spread are not established here, and it does not appear to be a tea drinkers commonly seek out by name.
